rows.context: A chemical UV filter absorbed through skin
rows.swap: A mineral (zinc oxide) sunscreen
rows.note: Octinoxate is a chemical filter with hormone-disruption questions and measurable skin absorption. Mineral zinc-oxide sunscreens sit on the skin and avoid the issue while still protecting you — sun protection still matters.

rows.name: Coloured Tattoo Ink (Metals & PAHs)
rows.context: Pigmented tattoo inks deposited permanently in the skin
rows.swap: A reputable artist using REACH-compliant, disclosed inks
rows.note: Some coloured inks contain heavy metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and the pigment stays in skin and lymph nodes for life. Choosing a professional using regulated inks reduces what goes in.

rows.name: Fresh Latex Paint (VOCs)
rows.context: Newly painted interior walls off-gassing solvents
rows.swap: Zero- or low-VOC paint, with windows open while it cures
rows.note: Conventional paint releases volatile organic compounds for days to weeks after application. Zero-VOC formulas plus ventilation dramatically cut what you breathe.

rows.name: Vinyl Mini-Blinds (Lead Dust)
rows.context: Imported PVC window blinds that degrade in sunlight
rows.swap: Aluminium, wood, or certified lead-free blinds
rows.note: Older or imported PVC blinds can be stabilised with lead, which forms a fine dust on the surface as the plastic ages in sunlight. Non-PVC blinds avoid it entirely.

rows.name: Air-Conditioner & HVAC Mould
rows.context: Mould growing on damp cooling coils and filters, then circulated
rows.swap: Regular filter changes, coil cleaning and fixing condensation
rows.note: Damp air-handling equipment can grow mould whose spores are then blown through the home. Routine maintenance and controlling moisture keep it from spreading.

rows.name: In-Tank Toilet Cleaner Tablets
rows.context: Chlorine-releasing tablets sitting in the toilet cistern
rows.swap: A brush plus vinegar or an as-needed bowl cleaner
rows.note: In-tank tablets slowly release chlorine chemicals into standing water and the bathroom air. Manual cleaning as needed avoids a constant low-level release.

rows.name: Aerosol Oven Cleaner (Lye Fumes)
rows.context: Caustic spray oven cleaner used in an enclosed kitchen
rows.swap: A baking-soda paste left overnight, then wiped
rows.note: Spray oven cleaners atomise sodium hydroxide and solvents that are corrosive to airways. A baking-soda paste does the same job without the caustic mist.

rows.name: Chemical Drain Cleaner
rows.context: Lye- or acid-based liquid drain openers
rows.swap: A drain snake, plunger or enzyme-based opener
rows.note: Strong chemical drain cleaners are highly corrosive and can release fumes or splash. Mechanical tools and enzyme products clear most clogs without the hazard.

rows.name: Fabric & Upholstery Stain Cleaner
rows.context: Solvent-based spot cleaners for carpets and sofas
rows.swap: Water-based cleaners or a DIY vinegar solution
rows.note: Many spot cleaners rely on volatile solvents and sometimes fluorinated repellents that linger in soft furnishings. Water-based options cut the residual off-gassing.

rows.name: Cigarette Smoking (Firsthand)
rows.context: Directly inhaling tobacco combustion products
rows.swap: Evidence-based cessation support and nicotine-replacement
rows.note: Firsthand tobacco smoke is one of the largest avoidable exposures there is, delivering thousands of toxicants including known carcinogens. Cessation services meaningfully improve the odds of quitting.

rows.name: Charcoal Grill Briquettes (PAH Smoke)
rows.context: Fat dripping onto hot charcoal, coating food in smoke
rows.swap: Lump charcoal or gas, and avoid charring the food
rows.note: Flare-ups and heavy smoke deposit polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons on grilled food. Lower heat, trimming fat and avoiding charring reduce how much forms.

rows.name: Gas-Powered Leaf Blower (2-Stroke)
rows.context: Standing behind a two-stroke engine that burns oil with fuel
rows.swap: A battery-electric leaf blower
rows.note: Two-stroke engines burn a fuel-oil mix inefficiently, producing high levels of unburned hydrocarbons and fine particles right at head height. Battery models eliminate the exhaust.

rows.name: Fireworks Smoke (Perchlorate & Metals)
rows.context: Standing downwind of consumer fireworks
rows.swap: Watch from a distance, upwind
rows.note: Firework smoke carries perchlorate and metal particulates that briefly spike local air pollution. Watching from upwind and at a distance limits what you inhale.

rows.name: Hookah / Shisha Smoke
rows.context: Water-pipe tobacco smoked over a long session
rows.swap: Avoiding it — the water does not make it safe
rows.note: A hookah session can deliver more smoke, carbon monoxide and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons than a single cigarette. The water pipe cools the smoke but does not filter out the toxicants.

rows.name: Engineered Stone Countertop Dust
rows.context: Dry-cutting or drilling quartz countertops during a fit-out
rows.swap: Slabs cut off-site, or wet-cutting with on-tool dust extraction
rows.note: Engineered 'quartz' stone is typically over 90% crystalline silica, against 40–50% for granite. Dry-cutting it releases respirable silica that permanently scars the lungs; hundreds of silicosis cases have been counted among fabricators. Householders are barely exposed unless a slab is dry-cut indoors.

studies.claim: California surveillance (2019-2022) found 52 silicosis cases among engineered-stone countertop fabricators; 10 (19%) were fatal, at a median age at death of 46.
Engineered stone is over 90% crystalline silica by weight, against 40-50% for granite and under 10% for marble.

rows.name: Methylene Chloride Paint Stripper
rows.context: Solvent paint and coating removers used in a closed room
rows.swap: A benzyl-alcohol or soy-based stripper, or sanding with dust extraction
rows.note: Methylene chloride vapour displaces oxygen in the blood and has killed people refinishing bathtubs in unventilated spaces. US regulators banned it from consumer paint and coating removal in 2019 and tightened the remaining uses under a 2024 risk-management rule.

rows.name: Coal-Tar Driveway Sealant (PAHs)
rows.context: Black sealer coating a drive, path or parking lot
rows.swap: An asphalt-based sealer, or leaving the surface unsealed
rows.note: Coal-tar sealcoat is loaded with polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Worn particles track indoors on shoes and tyres: US Geological Survey sampling found PAH in house dust about 25 times higher in homes beside coal-tar-sealed lots than beside plain asphalt or concrete.

rows.name: Ozone-Generating Air Purifiers
rows.context: 'Ionic' or ozone air cleaners run in an occupied room
rows.swap: A true-HEPA purifier with activated carbon, and open windows
rows.note: Ozone is a lung irritant, and the EPA's review concluded these devices do not control indoor pollutants effectively at concentrations that stay below public-health limits. Some ionisers also make ozone as a by-product, then sell the resulting smell as 'fresh air' when it is the irritant itself.

studies.claim: Ionization and ozonolysis air purifiers tested in offices, bathrooms, bedrooms and cars often produced ozone concentrations well in excess of public and/or industrial safety levels set by US EPA, California ARB and OSHA.

rows.name: Vermiculite Attic Insulation (Asbestos)
rows.context: Loose grey-brown pebble insulation in a pre-1990 attic
rows.swap: Leaving it sealed and undisturbed; an accredited asbestos contractor if it must move
rows.note: A single Montana mine supplied over 70% of US vermiculite between 1919 and 1990 and its ore was contaminated with asbestos, so vermiculite loft insulation from that era — often sold as Zonolite — should be assumed to contain it. Undisturbed it releases little; disturbing it during DIY is the risk.

studies.claim: Workers who mined and processed the asbestos-contaminated Libby vermiculite died significantly more often of asbestosis (SMR 165.8), lung cancer (SMR 1.7) and mesothelioma, rising with cumulative exposure.

In tests in three homes, airborne amphibole asbestos was not elevated when Zonolite attic insulation was undisturbed; cleaning, remodeling and other activities that disturbed it produced significant airborne concentrations.
In homes with vermiculite attic insulation or other asbestos materials, amphibole asbestos was detected in the living space of 12 (26%) of the homes tested, chrysotile in 45 (98%).
Among 198 adults exposed to Libby amphibole only in childhood and adolescence, 96 (48%) had pleural thickening as adults, with likelihood rising with years lived in the area.
In rats inhaling Libby amphibole for 13 weeks, lung fibre burdens declined only gradually over 18 months, and inflammation and interstitial fibrosis persisted up to 18 months after exposure.

sources.name: US EPA — Protect your family from asbestos-contaminated vermiculite insulation (updated 2026-04-17)
US EPA — My attic has vermiculite insulation in it. Am I at risk? (updated 2026-07-20)
US DOE — Energy Renovations: Insulation, a guide for contractors to share with homeowners (May 2012), Table 2.2

guidance.title: If it is in your attic
steps: Recognise it: a pebble-like, pour-in insulation, usually grey-brown or silver-gold, often sold as Zonolite.
Assume it contains asbestos. EPA says further testing is not needed to take the right precautions.
Leave it undisturbed. Do not store boxes in that attic, and do not let children play there.

Do not remove it yourself. Before any remodelling or renovation that would disturb it, or if it must come out, hire a trained, accredited asbestos contractor — EPA advises one independent of the firm that assessed it.
Its insulating value: about R-2.7 per inch of depth, per a 2012 US Department of Energy guide for contractors.

rows.name: Titanium Dioxide (E171) in Food
rows.context: A white colourant in sweets, icing, sauces and supplements
rows.swap: Products with no 'titanium dioxide' or 'E171' on the ingredient list
rows.note: In 2021 the European food-safety regulator concluded E171 can no longer be considered safe as a food additive, because genotoxicity could not be ruled out and the particles accumulate slowly in the body. The EU withdrew it from food; it is still permitted in the US, so labels are worth reading.

studies.claim: EFSA's panel could not rule out a genotoxicity concern for TiO2 particles and concluded E 171 can no longer be considered safe as a food additive.
Gastrointestinal absorption of TiO2 particles is low, but they may accumulate in the body.

rows.name: Red Dye No. 3 (Erythrosine)
rows.context: A bright cherry-red synthetic colour in sweets and drinks
rows.swap: Colour from beetroot, paprika extract or carmine
rows.note: The US regulator revoked its authorisation in January 2025 — as a point of law, not of demonstrated human harm. The Delaney Clause forbids any additive that causes cancer in animals, and the agency stated plainly that the rat mechanism involved does not occur in people. A low priority next to real exposures.

rows.name: Brominated Vegetable Oil (Citrus Sodas)
rows.context: A flavour stabiliser in some citrus-flavoured soft drinks
rows.swap: Sparkling water with fresh citrus, or any soda not listing BVO
rows.note: BVO kept citrus flavouring from separating out, at up to 15 parts per million. In July 2024 the US regulator revoked the authorisation after studies run with the NIH found the potential for adverse effects in humans; bromine accumulates in fat. Most drinks makers had already reformulated.

studies.claim: In a 90-day feeding study, rats given 0.1% and 0.5% BVO in their diet developed thyroid follicular cell hypertrophy, with raised TSH at the highest dose; the authors name the thyroid as a potential target organ.
In the same 90-day rat study, di- and tetra-bromostearic acid built up in the heart, liver and inguinal fat in a clear dose-response.

rows.name: Parabens in Cosmetics
rows.context: Preservatives in lotions, shampoos and make-up
rows.swap: Products preserved with phenoxyethanol or sodium benzoate
rows.note: The longer-chain parabens are the ones regulators acted on: the EU caps propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14% and bars them from leave-on nappy-area products for under-threes, on weak oestrogenic-activity grounds. Methyl- and ethylparaben are better tolerated and still permitted at higher levels.

rows.name: Homosalate Sunscreen
rows.context: A chemical UV filter in daily face and body sunscreen
rows.swap: A mineral zinc-oxide sunscreen, or a filter such as Tinosorb
rows.note: After an EU scientific committee flagged possible endocrine activity, the permitted level was cut from 10% to 7.34% and restricted to face products. It is still allowed at 10% elsewhere, including the US. Do not stop using sunscreen over this — change the filter instead.

rows.name: Locally Caught Freshwater Fish
rows.context: Fish taken from local rivers and lakes rather than bought
rows.swap: Check your state, Tribal or territory fish advisory before eating the catch
rows.note: In July 2024 the EPA added twelve PFAS to the contaminants it recommends states and Tribes monitor in locally caught freshwater fish, and says its national fish-tissue survey has found PFAS at levels that may affect health. Advisories are issued water by water, so which lake or river the fish came from matters more than the species.

sources.name: US EPA news release, 11 July 2024, 'EPA Releases New Science-Based Recommendations to Help More States, Tribes, and Territories Reduce Exposure to PFAS in Fish'
US EPA, 'Meaningful and Achievable Steps You Can Take to Reduce Your Risk'

studies.claim: In over 500 composite fillet samples from US EPA monitoring (2013-2015), median total PFAS was 9,500 ng/kg in rivers and streams and 11,800 ng/kg in the Great Lakes, 278 times the levels FDA found in commercially relevant fish; PFOS averaged 74% of the total.

In US EPA's national surveys of fish fillets from 164 urban river and 157 Great Lakes sites, PFOS was the most frequently detected perfluorinated compound, at up to 127 ng/g in rivers and 80 ng/g in the Great Lakes.

EFSA's contaminants panel judged effects on the immune system the most critical for PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS and PFOS, set a tolerable weekly intake of 4.4 ng/kg body weight for their sum, and concluded that parts of the European population exceed it.
After residents of Ronneby, Sweden, stopped drinking PFAS-contaminated water, their mean serum half-lives were estimated at 5.3 years for PFHxS, 3.4 years for PFOS and 2.7 years for PFOA.

rows.name: Sewage-Sludge Fertiliser on Garden Soil
rows.context: Biosolids spread or sold as a soil conditioner or fertiliser
rows.swap: A soil amendment whose feedstock is stated on the bag, or compost you make yourself
rows.note: The EPA released a draft risk assessment on 14 January 2025 covering PFOA and PFOS in sewage sludge that is land-applied as a soil conditioner or fertiliser. It is a draft that went out for public comment, not a rule, so the useful response is knowing what an amendment is made from rather than treating any number as settled.

sources.name: US EPA, 'Draft Sewage Sludge Risk Assessment for Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) and Perfluorooctane Sulfonic Acid (PFOS)', released 14 Jan 2025, EPA 820-P-25-001, Docket EPA-HQ-OW-2024-0504

rows.name: Fluorinated Plastic Containers
rows.context: Fluorine-treated HDPE bottles holding household and garden liquids
rows.swap: The same product in an untreated container; ask the maker whether the bottle is fluorinated
rows.note: Treating a plastic bottle with fluorine to stop it leaking or swelling can form PFAS on the inner wall. EPA testing detected eight PFAS in rinsate from fluorinated HDPE containers at 20 to 50 parts per billion, and its September 2022 study found they leach into the liquid stored inside and keep leaching the longer it sits. The EPA says such containers are used for household consumer, pesticide, fuel and automotive products.

sources.name: US EPA, 'Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Pesticide and Other Packaging' (page updated 3 Nov 2025; container leaching study 8 Sept 2022; TSCA s.21 petition granted 10 July 2024)

studies.claim: A directly fluorinated container held about 64 ng/g of PFAS; 7-day leaching into water, solvents and foods released 0.99-66.92 ng/g, up to 830% more at elevated temperature, mostly short-chain PFCAs.

Multiple studies link PFAS exposure to adverse immune outcomes in children, and dyslipidemia is the strongest metabolic outcome; cancer evidence is limited to manufacturing locations with extremely high exposures.

unsourced.reason: The PFAS measured here are mainly short-chain or fluorotelomer compounds; the human half-life studies found cover long-chain PFAS (PFOS, PFOA, PFHxS), so none is cited.

rows.name: Dairy from PFAS-Affected Farmland
rows.context: Milk and dairy from livestock grazing land carrying PFAS
rows.swap: Where a local advisory names affected farms, dairy sourced outside that area
rows.note: The EPA lists dairy products from livestock exposed to PFAS among the routes by which PFAS reach food, alongside fish from contaminated water, and notes that biosolids used on agricultural land can affect animals that graze it. The pathway runs through the land, so it surfaces near known contamination rather than everywhere.

sources.name: US EPA, 'Our Current Understanding of the Human Health and Environmental Risks of PFAS' (page updated 14 July 2026)

studies.claim: At 22 Swedish dairy farms within 10 km of PFAS contamination hotspots, PFOA, PFOS and PFNA were found in 5-77% of milk samples and one exceeded the EU indicative level for PFOA; all PFAS were below detection in milk from 20 regional dairies.

EFSA's contaminants panel judged effects on the immune system the most critical for PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS and PFOS, set a tolerable weekly intake of 4.4 ng/kg body weight for their sum, and concluded that parts of the European population exceed it.
After residents of Ronneby, Sweden, stopped drinking PFAS-contaminated water, their mean serum half-lives were estimated at 5.3 years for PFHxS, 3.4 years for PFOS and 2.7 years for PFOA.
